title: Malformed autonomy-health path payloads degrade to the current directory and can pass the launch gate
observed_behavior: The CLI accepts any JSON mapping, including an empty object, as a resolved-path contract. Every missing required path is converted by _path to Path(), which resolves operationally as the current directory, while missing optional paths and malformed config_data are silently normalized. The resulting health payload has overall_status review rather than blocked, and main returns exit code 0 because it rejects only a blocked status.
expected_invariant: A launch gate must reject a missing or structurally invalid resolved-path contract with a nonzero error and must never substitute the process current directory for required app, workspace, pipeline, configuration, audit, or rerun paths.
root_cause: _read_payload validates only that the JSON root is a mapping; resolved_paths_from_payload has no required-field or type validation; and _path deliberately maps blank values to Path(). The CLI then treats every non-blocked result, including review caused by an unusable contract, as success.
failure_scenario: A caller emits {}, omits one or more required keys, or sends blank values after a serialization/integration regression. The gate scans relative to the Codex or launcher working directory, reports review, and exits 0, allowing unattended launch to proceed without validating the intended pipeline paths.
evidence: Current autonomy_health_gate.py SHA-256 is 8a880d3c02c0fb5ad90e91f7e2129e2f4ed4e43fe59f5231dbf870e1bafa0ed5; lines 24-71 implement the permissive normalization and lines 93-104 return 0 for every non-blocked health result.
A read-only current-tree probe invoked main([--paths-json, {}]); it returned exit code 0 with overall_status review and no blocker codes.

Current autonomy_health.py SHA-256 is 7d6dd566e2e602ea6b6abe1a750008747e5e59484dd68d42bda05597c07cb6f9; autonomy_health_is_blocked checks only for the literal blocked status, so review is not a launch blocker.

Focused autonomy growth/soak tests have SHA-256 values 2c6b8f8339a8e176b576183125abd53b88154e94803eecfc78016d72b26749c9 and f7f515d239d546bd9d91b427069bc2ec6593611f0e04c9282bb8917d1ee4c365; they construct complete payloads and do not exercise an empty or partial mapping.
Broad current-worker deduplication found only W03-006, which concerns malformed persisted progress JSON in runtime health, not malformed path-contract acceptance at this CLI boundary.
existing_safeguards: Missing raw JSON, syntactically invalid JSON, and a non-object JSON root raise and return exit code 2; blocked health returns exit code 76.
safeguard_gap: A syntactically valid object has no schema validation, and review is treated as success even when the object lacks every required path.
tests_present: Growth snapshot and soak-tick tooling tests cover complete resolved-path payloads and normal health results.
The CLI error wrapper covers exceptions raised after parsing.
tests_missing: Empty-object and partial-object CLI cases asserting exit code 2.
Blank, non-string, and wrong-type required path fields.
A regression assertion that required paths can never resolve from Path() or the process current directory.
recommended_remediation: Validate the payload against the complete ResolvedPaths input contract before constructing it: require nonblank path strings for every mandatory field, validate config_data types, and return the structured error exit for contract violations. Consider treating an unusable review state as nonzero at this launch-gate boundary.
remediation_risk: medium: callers relying on permissive partial payloads will fail fast and must be updated, but no valid complete payload behavior needs to change
validation_rung: Focused autonomy-health gate unit/CLI tests for empty, partial, blank, and complete payloads; desktop launch-health integration smoke; existing autonomy growth and soak tests.
prior_audit_relationship: Related only at the health-gating outcome; W03-006 has a different input, implementation, and root cause.

title: code_read returns an oversized first line beyond its advertised byte cap and reports it as untruncated
observed_behavior: code_read enforces MAX_READ_BYTES only when selected is already nonempty. An oversized first requested line is therefore appended regardless of size. For a one-line file, returned_end equals the requested end, so truncated is false even though the response violated the 64 KiB response budget. The separate source-size limit permits this response to approach 2 MiB.
expected_invariant: Every successful code_read response must stay within its declared byte limit or return a structured oversized-line error, and the truncation indicator must truthfully identify every bounded response.
root_cause: The byte-limit guard is conditioned on selected, guaranteeing at least one whole line even when that line alone exceeds MAX_READ_BYTES. Truncation is derived only from returned line numbers and has no byte-exhaustion state.
failure_scenario: A minified JavaScript bundle, generated JSONL record, embedded data line, or otherwise long source line is requested through MCP. code_read emits far more than 64 KiB into the tool response and marks it complete, defeating the context/resource bound and potentially crowding out the audit or triggering transport/model limits.
evidence: Current code_context_service.py SHA-256 is c6ca62bf78f14fa6ca89e0e586533ced962266d5f3897ffba41e48706c021c12; constants declare a 65,536-byte read cap and 2,097,152-byte source cap, while lines 869-887 implement the first-line bypass and line-number-only truncation flag.
A disposable current-code probe requested a one-line 69,632-byte file. code_read returned ok true, 69,632 first-line bytes, line_count 1, and truncated false while MAX_READ_BYTES was 65,536.
Current test_code_context_mcp.py SHA-256 is 0e2e0c6bb383d9ba1090199514d6c68cb4aade1ff7f5207fc168f657d81f7ec2; its code_read coverage exercises line bounds but has no single-line byte-overflow case.
A bounded search of current worker fragments found no duplicate byte-limit root cause.
affected_flows: large generated or minified file inspection
existing_safeguards: The service caps ordinary reads at 400 lines, rejects source files larger than 2 MiB, rejects binary/non-UTF-8 files, and stops before adding a later line that would exceed the byte budget.
safeguard_gap: None of those safeguards bounds the first selected text line, and the response schema provides no oversized-line or byte-truncation signal.
tests_present: Line-range, path, binary, encoding, and ordinary bounded-read tests exist in the code-context test suite.
tests_missing: A first requested line larger than MAX_READ_BYTES.
A later oversized line after smaller selected lines.
Assertions over serialized response byte size and truthful truncated metadata.
recommended_remediation: Track byte truncation explicitly. If the first line exceeds the response budget, return a structured line_too_large error or a deliberately chunked representation with an omitted-byte count; never append content beyond MAX_READ_BYTES, and derive truncated from both line and byte exhaustion.
remediation_risk: low to medium: only oversized-line behavior and response metadata change, though MCP clients may need to handle a new structured error or chunk marker
validation_rung: Focused CodeContextService and MCP adapter tests with boundary-size, oversized-first-line, oversized-later-line, multibyte UTF-8, and serialization-size cases.
prior_audit_relationship: New current-audit root cause; no matching worker finding was present.

title: A failing Tdarr sample run prunes older proof before returning its failure status
observed_behavior: command_run_samples accumulates fixture, preparation, queue, source-hash, processing, classification, and containment findings, writes the current report, and then unconditionally invokes prune_run_roots whenever keep_last is at least one. Only after older sentinel-marked roots have been recursively removed does it calculate and return exit_code_for_findings. A critical or error-bearing newest run therefore counts toward retention and can evict the most recent successful proof.
expected_invariant: Retention cleanup described as occurring after a successful run must not destroy older successful evidence until the new run has passed its finding policy and is eligible to replace it.
root_cause: The destructive retention call is sequenced before success is calculated and is not conditional on the finding-derived exit code, report-only policy, or an explicit successful-run marker. prune_run_roots orders solely by modification time and sentinel presence, not proof validity.
failure_scenario: With keep_last=1, one valid prior run exists and a new run produces critical findings. The new failed run is newest, so pruning deletes the valid prior run and retains only the failed evidence; the command then exits nonzero after the irreversible deletion.
evidence: Current tdarr_matrix_reporting.py SHA-256 is 17ed760b937cfe0695cfb9b8f5d3212d04e6e307a6d6e7c592a2a5b083712693; lines 273-305 gather/write findings, lines 320-321 prune, and line 323 computes the failure exit afterward.

Current tdarr_matrix_operations.py SHA-256 is 2e85173b869ff858a830d977c8ead9b54e5f0d2af1443fdd78af2ec81013227e; prune_run_roots sorts sentinel roots by modification time, removes all but the newest keep_last, and does not inspect audit outcome.

Current test_tdarr_matrix_audit.py SHA-256 is 455de22ef1a2b828840cbe95709218392e62861995cf8d774054232e98ef5d19; it tests direct prune mechanics and canonical-root rails but does not exercise command_run_samples with failing findings plus keep_last.
A bounded current-worker deduplication search found no matching failed-run retention finding.
existing_safeguards: Pruning is restricted to the canonical TdarrMatrixRuns root, requires a sentinel on each direct child, retains at least one root, and supports dry-run preview.
safeguard_gap: The rails protect path scope and the newest directory, but do not establish that the newest directory is successful evidence worthy of replacing older proof.
tests_present: Direct pruning tests cover canonical root enforcement, sentinel eligibility, ordering, keep_last, and dry-run behavior.
tests_missing: command_run_samples with a failed current run and keep_last enabled.
Retention semantics for prior successful versus current failed roots.
An assertion that destructive prune is not called before exit policy is known.
recommended_remediation: Compute the finding-derived exit status before retention. Invoke destructive pruning only when the current run meets the success policy, or retain successful runs in a separately marked/indexed set so a failed run cannot displace the last passing proof. Keep dry-run available independently.
remediation_risk: low: command ordering and retention eligibility change; run execution and report contents remain unchanged
validation_rung: Focused Tdarr reporting tests using disposable canonical-shaped roots and mocked processing outcomes, covering successful, failed, report-only, dry-run, and keep_last variants.
prior_audit_relationship: New current-audit root cause; no matching worker finding was present.

title: Proof Pack rebuild recursively deletes any caller-selected directory that contains a same-named sentinel
observed_behavior: The materialize CLI accepts an arbitrary absolute or repository-relative --proof-root. On --rebuild, prepare_proof_root authorizes recursive deletion solely by the existence of a child whose name matches TDARR_PROOF_PACK_SENTINEL; it neither restricts the root to the canonical proof-pack location/allowed parent nor validates sentinel contents or root identity. shutil.rmtree then deletes the selected directory and all children.
expected_invariant: A recursive rebuild must prove that the resolved target is the intended canonical Proof Pack root, or a tightly bounded explicitly allowed disposable root, using a trustworthy root-identity marker before any deletion.
root_cause: A same-named sentinel file is treated as sufficient authorization for shutil.rmtree, while resolve_path and the public CLI deliberately permit unrestricted targets. No canonical-parent assertion, root identity payload, path-depth check, or deletion plan confirmation bridges that gap.
failure_scenario: An operator supplies the wrong --proof-root, reuses/copies a directory that happens to contain the sentinel, or encounters a planted/stale sentinel in a valuable directory, then adds --rebuild. The entire directory is recursively deleted before source-manifest validation or proof materialization can fail.
evidence: Current tdarr_proof_pack.py SHA-256 is 98b4763d8d9678a96cbd7a7e101f5843699a13e86222501b22288e7717079292; lines 42-46 accept arbitrary paths, lines 128-138 authorize/deletes by sentinel name alone, and lines 506-550 expose that path with --rebuild.

A probe confined to TemporaryDirectory created victim/keep.txt plus a sentinel containing unrelated text, then called prepare_proof_root(victim, rebuild=True). It returned already_exists false, recreated an empty victim root, and keep.txt did not survive.

Current test_tdarr_proof_pack.py SHA-256 is 824d2313b0c13056adc1a1edf652c9e0ebf28aa355090a335076aea13b3b0636; tests use disposable arbitrary proof roots for normal behavior but do not assert canonical/allowed-root rejection or trusted sentinel identity before rebuild.
A bounded current-worker deduplication search found no matching Proof Pack arbitrary-root deletion finding.
existing_safeguards: The command requires explicit --rebuild for nonempty roots and refuses a nonempty root that lacks the expected sentinel filename.
safeguard_gap: The sentinel is forgeable and unvalidated, and it says nothing about whether the selected directory is within an allowed parent. Explicit rebuild intent does not authorize an unbounded target.
tests_present: Normal materialize, verification, and cleanup flows are tested inside disposable directories.
Nonempty roots without the sentinel are refused.
tests_missing: Rejection of a --proof-root outside the canonical or explicitly allowed scratch parent.
Malformed, copied, or wrong-root sentinel content.
Boundary checks for parent/root aliases and symlink or junction resolution before recursive deletion.
recommended_remediation: Before deletion, resolve the target and require it to equal the canonical Proof Pack root or fall under an explicit safe scratch allowlist. Store and validate a versioned sentinel payload containing root identity/purpose, reject links/reparse escapes, and preferably rename the old root to a recoverable quarantine before rebuilding. Preserve the disposable-root injection only behind an internal test API.
remediation_risk: medium: tests and bespoke developer workflows using arbitrary roots will need an explicit safe-root override, but the production data-loss surface is narrowed
validation_rung: High-risk filesystem validation in disposable directories: canonical root, allowed test root, outside-root rejection, malformed/copied sentinel, symlink/junction escape, rebuild rollback, and existing Proof Pack verification tests.
prior_audit_relationship: New current-audit destructive-boundary root cause; no matching worker finding was present.

title: Git command failures are serialized as an unknown but falsely clean release identity
observed_behavior: _git_text catches every exception from Git and returns the same empty string used for legitimate empty output. source_revision converts that to unknown, but source_dirty converts it to False. resolve_release_identity then emits a semver without the dirty suffix, and build_manifest writes source_dirty false, so a timeout, missing Git executable, invalid repository, permission failure, or Git process error is represented as a clean tree.
expected_invariant: Release provenance must distinguish a successfully observed clean tree from an unavailable/failed Git status. A release manifest must fail closed or record an explicit unknown/error state; it must never assert source_dirty false without a successful status command.
root_cause: The shared string helper erases command outcome and stderr by broadly catching Exception. Two callers then assign different fallbacks to the same ambiguous empty string, with source_dirty choosing the safety-sensitive clean boolean.
failure_scenario: A release is built where Git is unavailable, times out, or cannot read the worktree. Packaging continues with source_revision unknown, source_dirty false, and a tool_semver lacking .dirty; downstream consumers and operators can treat uncommitted or unverifiable content as a clean reproducible release.
evidence: Current release_identity.py SHA-256 is 4fee68cabd8f7b030fe0018e963ae5ebe5605a8ce7208590f0b8b1189c90cc53; lines 100-121 collapse all Git failures to empty text/false and lines 133-145 propagate the result.

A read-only mock probe made subprocess.run raise OSError. source_revision returned unknown, source_dirty returned false, and resolve_release_identity emitted identity_dirty false with tool_semver 0.0.0+2026.07.21.001.gunknown.
Current build_release_manifest.py SHA-256 is 077451beb1324db7aeeeb58dba2cc607efe0ac47f36972e48bdfca2ca35d0247; build_manifest records identity.source_dirty directly in release metadata.

Current test_change_control.py SHA-256 is 3a03979e6d9087c41889c075b7b88c19f7509400d43c9ea2373f633d1bc6d417; its manifest test asserts only that source_revision and source_dirty keys exist, not their behavior under Git failure.
W10-013 was inspected after broad deduplication; it concerns version/tag/commit binding in a GitHub workflow before asset clobber, not local Git failure being mislabeled clean.
existing_safeguards: Git commands use check=True and a five-second timeout, and an unavailable revision is labeled unknown.
safeguard_gap: All safeguard-triggered exceptions are swallowed, and only the revision field exposes uncertainty; the more safety-sensitive dirty flag asserts false and the semver appears clean.
tests_present: Change-control tests verify manifest construction and the presence of release identity keys under normal execution.
tests_missing: Missing Git executable, timeout, nonzero Git exit, invalid repository, and permission-error cases.
An invariant that source_dirty false is emitted only after successful status.
Release-manifest fail-closed or explicit-unknown behavior when provenance cannot be established.
recommended_remediation: Return a structured Git result or let command failures propagate. Represent dirty state as true/false/unknown internally; require a successful status before false, and make release manifest generation fail on unknown for release channels unless an explicit development-only override records the uncertainty in metadata and tool_semver.
remediation_risk: medium: release tooling may newly fail in source archives or Git-less environments and will need an explicit documented override path
validation_rung: Focused release_identity and build_release_manifest tests mocking clean, dirty, empty-repo, missing-Git, timeout, and nonzero-exit outcomes; then change-control/release manifest validation.
prior_audit_relationship: Distinct from W10-013: this finding concerns local provenance observation failure being serialized as clean, not workflow-level version/tag/asset identity checks.
